title: Presentation independence and base-change calculus for the obstruction ideal
statement: Let $R$ be Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $B$ a finitely presented commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For the ideals of [def-per-gabber-ramero-obstruction-ideal], $H_{B/R}=H_P$ for every finite polynomial presentation $P\twoheadrightarrow B$. Its vanishing set in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is exactly the locus where $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. If $R\to R'$ is any homomorphism to a Noetherian ring and $B'=B\otimes_RR'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], then $H_{B/R}B'\subseteq H_{B'/R'}$. If $B\to C$ is a smooth finitely presented algebra map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], then $H_{B/R}C\subseteq H_{C/R}$.

proof.text: For each presentation write $M_P\xrightarrow{\delta_P}F_P$. The polynomial Kähler-basis node identifies $B\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ with $F_P=B^{\oplus n}$ by $1\otimes\mathrm dx_i\mapsto e_i$, and under it $1\otimes\mathrm df\mapsto(\pi(\partial f/\partial x_i))_i$, so the conormal map of the homotopy node is the map $\delta_P$ of the obstruction-ideal definition. The homotopy-equivalence node gives maps $\varphi_i:P\to Q$, $\psi_i:Q\to P$ on the two conormal complexes and $k:F_P\to M_P$ with $1-\psi_1\varphi_1=k\delta_P$. If $h_Q\delta_Q=b1$, put $h_P=\psi_1h_Q\varphi_0+bk$. Then $h_P\delta_P=b\psi_1\varphi_1+b(1-\psi_1\varphi_1)=b1$. Reverse $P,Q$ to obtain $H_P=H_Q$. Each is an ideal: add witnessing maps, multiply them by scalars, and use the zero map. Thus their intersection in the obstruction-ideal definition equals each $H_P$. Choose henceforth a finite presentation whose kernel $I$ has finite generators $f_1,\ldots,f_m$, as supplied by finite presentation.

Suppose $b\in H_P$ lies outside a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$, witnessed by $h\delta=b1_M$. Over $B_b$, $b^{-1}h$ is a left inverse. The principal-localization conormal node, read through the Kähler basis $1\otimes\mathrm dx_i$ of the polynomial Kähler-basis node, identifies the complex of the finite presentation $P[t]\twoheadrightarrow B_b$, $t\mapsto b^{-1}$, with $[M_b\to F_b]\oplus[B_b\xrightarrow{b}B_b]$. The first summand has the left inverse just given and the second has inverse multiplication by $b^{-1}$. This presentation has kernel generated by the $f_j$ and $\widetilde b t-1$, with $\widetilde b\in P$ lifting $b$. The split-conormal smoothness node therefore makes $B_b$ smooth over $R$. By the affine smoothness comparison node, $\operatorname{Spec}B_b\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth; identifying $\operatorname{Spec}B_b$ with the principal open $D(b)\ni\mathfrak q$, clauses (c) and (b) of the open-restriction node make $D(b)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ smooth. Consequently every prime outside $V(H_P)$ has an open neighbourhood on which $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth.

Conversely let $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be smooth on an open $W\ni\mathfrak q$. Choose $a\notin\mathfrak q$ with $D(a)\subseteq W$; clauses (a) and (c) of the open-restriction node make $\operatorname{Spec}B_a\cong D(a)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ smooth, and the affine smoothness comparison node makes $R\to B_a$ a smooth ring map. The smooth-localization conormal node gives $h_a:F_a\to M_a$ with $h_a\delta_a=1$. Choose a common denominator for its values on the finite basis of $F$: for some $r\geq0$ choose $h:F\to M$ with $h/1=a^rh_a$. The map $h\delta-a^r1_M$ is zero after localization. The classes of the finite list $f_j$ generate $M$; for each of them choose a power of $a$ killing its image under that difference, and let $s$ be the largest of those exponents. Then $a^sh\delta=a^{r+s}1_M$. Thus $a^{r+s}\in H_P$ and it lies outside $\mathfrak q$. If $m=0$, take $s=0$. This proves that $V(H_{B/R})$ is precisely the nonsmooth locus. Only finite lists of relations and of variables were used in the denominator argument.

proof.text: For base change put $P'=R'[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $I'=IP'$. There is a presentation $P'\twoheadrightarrow B'=B\otimes_RR'$ with kernel $I'$: its quotient represents exactly the same maps as the tensor product, since imposing the images of the $f_j$ imposes the original relations. There is a surjection $q:M\otimes_BB'\twoheadrightarrow M'=I'/I'^2$, $[f]\otimes c\mapsto c[f]$. It is onto because $I'$ is generated by images of $I$. With $F'=B'^n=F\otimes_BB'$, differentiation on generators gives $\delta'q=\delta\otimes1$. Given $h\delta=b1$, define $h'=q(h\otimes1)$. Then $h'\delta'q=q(h\delta\otimes1)=bq$; surjectivity of $q$ gives $h'\delta'=b1_{M'}$. Hence the image of $H_P$ is contained in $H_{P'}$, and its generated ideal is contained there. Step 1 identifies these ideals with $H_{B/R}$ and $H_{B'/R'}$. This argument uses a surjection, never an isomorphism, on the conormal modules.

source.place: Polynomial presentations and elementary tensor-product universal property; cf. Tag 00S1 functoriality

proof.text: For any $B$-module $N$, the extension-cokernel node identifies square-zero extension classes with the quotient of $\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,N)$ by maps through $\delta$. If $h\delta=b1_M$, then for every $v:M\to N$ one has $bv=(vh)\delta$; hence $b$ kills every such extension class. Conversely, if $b$ kills all extension classes for all $N$, use $N=M$ and the class represented by $1_M$: its being killed says exactly $b1_M=h\delta$ for some $h$. Thus $b\in H_P$ if and only if it annihilates every square-zero extension class, with no finiteness restriction on the coefficient module.

Let $B\to C$ be smooth as in the statement, $N$ any $C$-module, and $E$ an $R$-algebra square-zero extension of $C$ by $N$. Its pullback $E\times_C B$ is an extension of $B$ by the underlying $B$-module $N$. For $b\in H_{B/R}$, step 5 makes the pushout of this pullback by multiplication by $b$ split. Form instead the pushout $E_b$ of $E$ by multiplication by the image of $b$ in $C$. Its pullback to $B$ has the preceding split class. These pullback and pushout operations commute: on pairs the pullback is $(e,x)$ with $p(e)=f(x)$, and the kernel pushout imposes the same relations $j(n)=bn$ on the kernel in either order. Hence a splitting gives a map $B\to E_b$ over $B\to C$. Regard $E_b$ as a $B$-algebra by this map. The smooth square-zero lifting node, applied to $E_b\twoheadrightarrow C$ and $1_C$, gives a $B$-algebra section $C\to E_b$. Therefore $E_b$ is split and the image of $b$ kills the class of $E$.

proof.text: The composite $R\to C$ is finitely presented: adjoining finite generators for $C/B$ to those for $B/R$, and lifting the finite relations for $C/B$ to polynomials over the chosen presentation of $B$, gives finitely many relations over $R$. Thus the conormal definition and step 5 apply to $C/R$. Since step 6 works for every $C$-module $N$ and every extension, step 5 gives $\operatorname{image}(b)\in H_{C/R}$ for every $b\in H_{B/R}$. As $H_{C/R}$ is an ideal (step 1), it contains the extended ideal $H_{B/R}C$. Together with steps 1--4 this proves every clause.
